title: Auditing classes, Plato and Shakespeare, and two years without drink
summary: He audits classes in towns where he stays, reads philosophy with a dictionary, stops drinking and smoking for two years.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you do the paper work involved or did you just sit in on the lectures?
Well I'd sit in on the lectures and if they had any paper work I would write it down. You know what to do and I'd have to get a book naturally. So I asked the deans. You know, I'd read the books.
In other words, whenever you were in residence at it were in a town for any length or period and the town had a college.
in auditor, become an auditor in classes at that college?
What are some of the colleges that you did this at?
I can't remember them. There were so many of them. And the deans they were always so nice to me you know that I really wanted to learn.

Well yes, I can understand it because as a university professor myself I know what it is to have so many students in class today who are there because they are their parents status symbols you see. Not, they're not there because they want to learn as you did. Oh I'd be happy to have someone like you. (LAUGHTER).

That's right. And I bought a small edition of Shakespear's works. Those small pocket things used to carry them in my suitcase. And my dictionary, had to look up all the words to find out what they meant. And I would read those and I would read philosophy.
Do you have any idea of how many years you continued to do this?

Two years. I just quit drinking and smoking and really devoted myself to study and tried to improve naturally. And I think I did. I developed a fairly good vocabulary whenever I want to use it. But how often do you use that, what for? You know.
Well, I don't suppose that was the biggest thing that would come out of that because the biggest thing is what happens to you inside.
And the interest that it creates for you to continue no matter what you're doing in later life. I suppose you still enjoy reading and ....
